items.title: Check, Identify, Diagnose
items.description: A 3-step actionable sequence for vehicle owners.

items: Step 1: Check the fuel cap Is the fuel cap tight? If loose - tighten it. Drive for 50 miles. Light may clear.
Step 2: Identify the light Solid amber? → Schedule diagnostic (1-2 weeks) Flashing? → STOP DRIVING - immediate diagnostic Red? → STOP DRIVING - immediate diagnostic
Step 3: Book a diagnostic (£50-£150) A technician will read fault codes from the ECU, identify the specific issue, and provide a repair quote.

blocks.text: Important: “The codes tell the story. A reset without reading codes is pointless.”

items.title: ⚠️ Flashing Check Engine Light - Stop Driving
items.description: If your check engine light is flashing:

items: Pull over safely - Find a safe location
Turn off engine - Do not wait
Call for recovery - Do not drive
A flashing light means the engine is misfiring
Unburnt fuel is entering the exhaust system
This fuel destroys the catalytic converter (£500-£2,500)
Continuing to drive turns a £100 ignition repair into a £2,500 cat replacement

blocks.text: The flashing light danger: If your check engine light is flashing, unburnt fuel is entering the exhaust system and destroying your catalytic converter (£500-£2,500 repair).
A solid amber light means a non-urgent fault. You can drive short distances. Book a diagnostic within 1-2 weeks. But don't ignore it forever.
Red means a serious fault. Same as flashing - stop immediately.

items.title: Always Check Your Fuel Cap First
items.description: 💡 Always check your fuel cap first.

items: A loose cap triggers EVAP codes (P0455/P0457) This is the most common EML trigger (20% of all cases).
Tighten the cap and drive for 50 miles The light will usually clear automatically once the ECU confirms system pressure seal.
The EVAP system monitors fuel vapour leaks
A loose cap causes a vapour leak
The ECU detects the leak and illuminates the light
Tightening the cap seals the leak
The light clears after several drive cycles

blocks.question: What does the check engine light mean? +
blocks.answer: It means the ECU has detected a fault in the engine or emissions system. It could be minor (fuel cap) or serious (misfire).

blocks.question: Can I drive with the check engine light on? +
blocks.answer: Solid amber - yes, short distances. Flashing or red - no, stop immediately.

blocks.question: How much does check engine light diagnosis cost in the UK? +
blocks.answer: Check engine light diagnosis costs £50-£150 at UK independent garages. This includes reading fault codes.

blocks.question: Why is the check engine light flashing? +
blocks.answer: Active misfire. Unburnt fuel is destroying your catalytic converter. Stop driving immediately.

blocks.question: How long does it take for the check engine light to clear after fixing? +
blocks.answer: 50-100 miles of driving, or the garage can clear it with diagnostic equipment.

blocks.question: What's the most common cause of a check engine light? +
blocks.answer: A loose fuel cap (20% of cases). Always check it first.
